q: 1. Grid lines are parallel to ...............
options: magnetic meridian of the central point of the grid
line representing the central true meridian of the grid
explain: Grid lines in a coordinate system are typically aligned parallel to the central true meridian of that specific grid zone.

q: 2. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: For a WCB between 90 deg and 180 deg (SE quadrant), reduced bearing = N (180-WCB) E = N (180-120) E = N 60 E.

q: 3. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic isogonic line declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) are lines drawn through points of equal magnetic declination on a map.

q: 4. The horizon glass of the box sextant is ...............
options: concave in shape to from sharp image
explain: The horizon glass is half-silvered to allow the observer to see the horizon directly through the clear part and the reflected object in the silvered part.

q: 5. Isogonics lines are the lines having the same
explain: Isogonic lines join points on the earth's surface having equal magnetic declination.

q: 6. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place
options: is a constant for all bearings
explain: At a given station affected by local attraction, the same fixed correction applies to all bearings observed at that station, since all readings are equally displaced by the same disturbing influence.

q: 7. An instrumental error in compass survey is because of
options: no counter weight provision to counteract dip
local attraction due to bare current carrying conductors
explain: An instrumental error inherent to the compass itself (not due to external field conditions) is the lack of a counterweight arrangement to balance the dip of the needle in different magnetic latitudes.

q: 8. Quadrantal system confines the user to measure the bearings from
options: the north point or south point whichever is nearer
explain: In the Quadrantal (or Reduced) Bearing system, bearings are measured from North or South toward East or West, whichever side is closer, and never exceed 90°.

q: 9. The prismatic compass and surveyor's compass respectively give
options: whole circle bearing of a line & quadrantal bearing of a line
both quadrantal bearing of a line
both whole circle bearing of a line
quadrantal & whole circle bearing of a line
explain: Prismatic compasses are graduated 0-360° (WCB), while Surveyor's compasses are graduated in quadrants 0-90° (QB).

q: 10. The quadrantal bearing of a line is determined by
explain: The Surveyor's compass is specifically designed and graduated to give bearings in the quadrantal form (N/S - Angle - E/W).

q: 11. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place
explain: Local attraction affects the needle's orientation locally; however, the specific correction depends on the observed bearing's relationship to the magnetic interference.

q: 12. The W.C.B of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sing of correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrant.
explain: WCB is simpler for calculations because a single numerical value (0-360°) defines the direction without needing cardinal prefixes or suffixes.

q: 13. For a line AB
options: the fore bearing and back bearing of line AB differ by 180°
the fore bearing of AB and back bearing of line BA differ by 180°
explain: In a correct survey, the difference between the forward look (FB) and the backward look (BB) of the same line must be exactly 180°.

q: 14. Local attraction in a compass surveying may be due to
options: loss of magnetism in the needle
friction of the needle at the point
explain: Local attraction specifically refers to the deflection of the needle caused by nearby magnetic objects like iron ore, steel structures, or electric cables.

q: 15. The dip of the needle
options: varies from place to place & is zero at the equator and maximum at the poles
is zero at the equators and poles
explain: Magnetic dip is 0° at the magnetic equator (horizontal needle) and 90° at the magnetic poles (vertical needle).

q: 16. The Q. B of the lines are given by......, & ...... If W.C.B. of the lines are 0°, 135° & 270° respectively
explain: 0° is North (N), 135° is in the 2nd quadrant (180-135=S45°E), and 270° is due West (W90°).

q: 17. If the magnetic bearing of sun at noon at a place in southern hemisphere is 150°, the magnetic declination at that place is
explain: At noon, the sun is at the true meridian (180°). Declination = True Bearing (180°) - Magnetic Bearing (150°) = +30° (East).

q: 18. The magnetic declination at a place is 7°20' W, the bearing given by the compass is S45°40'E, the true bearing of the place is
explain: Convert S45°40'E to WCB: 180 - 45°40' = 134°20'. True Bearing = 134°20' - 7°20' (West) = 127°00'. Convert back to RB: 180 - 127 = S53°E.

q: 19. If the magnetic declination is (-) 6°0' and the reduced bearing of a line is S40°0'E the true bearing of the line is
explain: WCB = 180 - 40 = 140°. True WCB = 140 - 6 = 134°. True RB = 180 - 134 = S46°E. Note: Answer key 'd' indicates a specific calculation variant used in this text.

q: 20. Find the whole circle bearing of a line as shown in figure
explain: The diagram shows an angle of 15° West of North. WCB = 360 - 15 = 345°.

q: 21. The value of magnetic declination if the magnetic bearing of sun at noon is 350°
explain: True Bearing at noon = 360°/0°. Magnetic Bearing = 350°. Declination = 360 - 350 = 10° East.

q: 22. Back bearing of a line BA is 35° and bearing of BC is 125° then find the included angle ABC
explain: Included angle = 125° - 35° = 90°.

q: 23. The foremost work to be executed while traversing with a compass is
explain: Reconnaissance (preliminary inspection) is always the first step in any survey to plan station locations.

q: 24. Which one of the following may not be classified as natural error?
explain: A sluggish needle is an instrumental error caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, whereas the others are related to natural magnetic phenomena.

q: 25. The magnetic bearing of a line is 60° and true bearing of the same line is 70°. Find the declination
explain: Declination = True Bearing - Magnetic Bearing. 70° - 60° = +10°. A positive result indicates Eastern declination (10°E).

q: 26. If the station A and B are equally affected and in the different direction, then the difference between fore bearing and back bearing of a line AB should be
explain: If both stations are affected by local attraction, the 180° rule is violated; the resulting difference depends on the magnitude and direction of the local error at both ends.

q: 27. The maximum permissible difference allowed while taking down the fore bearing and back bearing of a line is
explain: In general practice for prismatic compass surveys, a discrepancy of up to 15 minutes is often considered acceptable before re-measurement is required.

q: 28. A horizontal angle which a line makes with the true meridian through one of the extremities of the line, is called
explain: When the reference meridian used is the true (geographic) meridian, the resulting horizontal angle is specifically called the true bearing of the line.

q: 29. The box of prismatic compass is made of
explain: The box of a prismatic compass is made of non-magnetic brass so that it does not interfere with or attract the freely suspended magnetic needle.

q: 30. If the end stations of a line are free from local attraction, then the difference in between fore and back bearing of that line should be
explain: In the absence of local attraction at either end station, the fore bearing and back bearing of a line always differ by exactly 180 degrees.

q: 31. The lines of force of earth's magnetic field are parallel to the earth's surface
options: at right angles to the poles
at 45 deg to the line joining poles
explain: Near the equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run roughly horizontal (parallel to the surface), which is why the dip of the needle is close to zero there; near the poles the field lines are nearly vertical.

q: 32. At magnetic poles, the dip of magnetic needle is
explain: At the magnetic poles, a freely suspended needle aligns itself vertically with the earth's field, giving a dip of 90 degrees.

q: 33. The least count of prismatic compass is
explain: A standard prismatic compass is generally graduated to allow readings to a least count of about 15 minutes of arc.

q: 34. The total number of zeroes graduated on a surveyor's compass is
explain: A surveyor's compass, graduated in the quadrantal bearing system, has two zero marks (at the North and South ends), unlike the prismatic compass which has only a single zero (North) on its whole-circle graduated ring.

q: 35. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: At the magnetic equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run horizontal, so a freely suspended needle shows zero dip.

q: 36. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its quadrant bearing is
explain: 120° lies in the second quadrant (SE). Quadrant Bearing = $180 - 120 = 60°$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 37. In the prismatic compass .............
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the needle and the graduated ring are attached; they remain stationary relative to the magnetic meridian while the box rotates.

q: 38. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to .............
options: incorrect leveling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic objects (iron ore, steel structures, power lines) interfering with the Earth's magnetic field.

q: 39. Azimuth (direct angles) is an angle measured in
explain: Azimuth is measured clockwise from the North (or South) meridian.

q: 40. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: clockwise or anticlockwise from North/South whichever is nearer...
explain: In the Reduced Bearing (RB) or Quadrantal system, bearings are measured from either North or South towards East or West, whichever is closer, ranging from 0° to 90°.

q: 41. In a whole circle bearing system N25°15'W corresponds to
explain: To convert N 25°15' W to WCB: 360° - 25°15' = 334°45' (since the bearing is in the 4th quadrant).

q: 42. If the fore bearing of a line is 36°15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since 36°15' is less than 180°, we add 180°: 36°15' + 180° = 216°15'.

q: 43. The zero of the graduated circle of prismatic compass is located at
explain: In a prismatic compass, the 0° mark is at the South end so that the reading under the prism (at the observer's end) correctly reflects the magnetic North bearing.

q: 44. The true meridian of a place is the line in which earth's surface in intersected by a plane through
explain: The true meridian is the great circle passing through the geographical North and South poles and the observer's position.

q: 45. During secular variation of magnetic meridian at different places
explain: Secular variation is a long-term swing (like a pendulum). Both the time it takes (period) and the total degree of swing (range) vary across centuries and locations.

q: 46. Isogonic lines are the lines having the same .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same.

q: 47. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its reduced bearing is .............
explain: A bearing of 120° is in the second quadrant (SE). $RB = 180 - 120 = 60$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 48. The reduced bearing of a line is N 87° W. Its whole bearing is .............
explain: N 87° W is in the fourth quadrant. $WCB = 360 - 87 = 273°$.

q: 49. When the magnetic declination is 5° 20' east, the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination (East is positive). At noon, True Bearing = 180°. $180° = MB + 5° 20'$. $MB = 174° 40'$.
